_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Accounting P1 (Financial Accounting), November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The optional
'information' field (array of lines) carries the INFORMATION block of each main question; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that main question and applies to all of its sub-questions.
The pre-printed ANSWER BOOK (paper1_answer_book.pdf) is tracked beside the paper.
memo_answer reproduces the marking guideline's figures and workings line by line (tick marks
removed; marking notes such as 'one part correct' kept). Unnumbered bullet sub-parts of a
question are kept in one entry with their marks added.
An ERRATA sheet issued with the paper is tracked as paper1_errata.pdf.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Fixed Assets and Internal Controls 25 marks 20 min; Q2 Concepts and
Statement of Comprehensive Income 50 marks 40 min; Q3 Statement of Financial Position and Notes 40
marks 30 min; Q4 Analysis and Interpretation of Financial Statements 35 marks 30 min. A Grade 11
Financial Indicator Formula Sheet is attached to the paper (not transcribed here).
ERRATA: the province's erratum notes that the answer book had too few lines under Operating expenses
for QUESTION 2.2, and directs that 2.2 be marked out of 40 instead of 45. The printed allocation (45)
is kept here so that the entries still sum to the printed paper total of 150.

questions.text: Calculate the missing figures denoted by (i) to (iv) in the fixed asset note.
questions.topic: Fixed assets: depreciation and the asset register
questions.memo_answer:

(ii) Carrying value of equipment at the beginning of the year: 600 000 - 180 000 = 420 000
(iii) Depreciation on equipment: Old 420 000 x 10/100 = 42 000; New 90 000 x 10/100 x 8/12 = 6 000; total 48 000 (one part correct)
(iv) Carrying value of vehicle disposed: 680 000 + 120 000 - 440 000 = 360 000; 360 000 x 12/100 x 10/12 = 36 000; 360 000 - 215 000 - 36 000 = 109 000 (one part correct)

questions.text: The owner notices that the mileage on one of the vehicles is extremely high. He therefore concluded that the driver is misusing the vehicle. Suggest TWO internal control measures that can be implemented to safeguard the business against the misuse of vehicles.
questions.topic: Internal control
questions.memo_answer:
Any TWO points:
• Signing in and out of vehicles to track where they are and who used them / putting tracking devices on the vehicles / have a log book to record the movement of vehicles.
• Have a policy on what time the vehicles should be returned to the business premises / lock them on business premises at night.

questions.text: • Explain whether the business is managing its operating activities efficiently. Quote TWO financial indicators with figures. (4) • Explain how the business can improve their sales in future. Quote ONE financial indicator. (2)
questions.topic: Analysis and interpretation of financial statements
questions.memo_answer:
Operating efficiency (4):
% operating profit on sales improved from 19,5% to 22,2%

questions.text: • The partners decided to increase their business activities in 2024 and agreed to take up a loan. Explain how their decision affected the financial risk of the business, quote ONE financial indicator with figures. (4) • Provide TWO suggestions that the partners can consider instead of increasing the loan. (2)
questions.topic: Analysis and interpretation of financial statements
questions.memo_answer:
Financial risk (4): Debt-equity ratio increased from 0,3 : 1 to 0,7 : 1. The business is now on high risk / relies too much on borrowed funds / debt has increased from 30% to 70% of own capital. (allocate part marks for incomplete answers)
Suggestions (2): Contributing more capital / increasing their capital contributions; Get another partner.

questions.text: Should the partners be satisfied with the % return on their investment? Explain and provide TWO points with relevant figures.
questions.topic: Analysis and interpretation of financial statements
questions.memo_answer:
Yes (or implied)
POINT 1: % return on capital increased from 22% to 27,1% (by 5,1% points)
POINT 2: % return on their investment exceeds interest on alternative investment (fixed deposit) of 8,5%
(Comparison to interest on alternative investment must be made or implied in the comment to get full marks.)

questions.text: Comment on the liquidity position of the business for 2024. Quote TWO financial indicators with comparative figures.
questions.topic: Analysis and interpretation of financial statements
questions.memo_answer:
Financial indicators with figures (any TWO):
• Current ratio decreased from 2 : 1 to 1,8 : 1
• Acid-test ratio increased from 0,8 : 1 to 0,9 : 1 but still indicating the problem of stock piling
• Debtors collection period increased from 32 to 56 days
• Stock turnover rate decreased from 8 times to 5,2 times a year
Comment on liquidity: Partners should be concerned about the liquidity position of their business as it will struggle to meet its short-term obligations - too much cash is tied up in stock / stock piling / debtors are taking too long to pay which could lead to liquidity problems / stock turnover rate declined showing a decline in the demand for products.
